_comment: Plugin manifest (authored by the plugin author). 'version' is the plugin semver (release-only); install-plugin reads 'setup'.
name: kaggle
description: Kaggle for Solaris agents through the official Kaggle CLI and six fixed, read-only reads through Kaggle's Python SDK for what the CLI drops, with a Kaggle project's master run only as an autocode agent (the autocode plugin, which this plugin requires: wakes, wake checks, watched jobs, reports): tools/kaggle.py is a stdlib gateway that pins the CLI (kaggle==2.2.4, with its tested kagglesdk==0.1.37 and a pinned six==1.17.0, which the CLI imports without naming it as a dependency) and installs it separately into each project (a folder with exactly one child folder holding an ai-pack manifest.json: the project's ai-pack folder, default aipack/, ai/ in older projects, any name) or ad-hoc task that uses it (<context>/.venv-kaggle, created on first call, rebuilt on a pin or package change, folder move or lost base Python; never global - at the bare framework root it runs from a throwaway uv environment; uv is found on PATH, in ~/.local/bin or in ~/.cargo/bin); with --sdk first it runs tools/kaggle_sdk.py in that same pinned environment instead of the CLI: topic <id> (one forum topic in full: the opening post as HTML with its links, and the nested reply tree, with a host flag for authors the forum badges as hosts, empty until the pinned SDK carries the author type), notebooks <slug> [--max N] (a competition's public notebooks with their best public scores, null when unknown) and account [--hours H] [--page-size N] [--done REF=TIME] (the signed-in account's quota, its own kernels and their run states, in one process), each printing one JSON document, and submissions <slug> [--page-size N] [--json] (the team's latest submissions with the error text competitions submissions drops) dataset <owner/slug> [--json] (a dataset's current version number and every version) and kernel <owner/slug> [--json] (a kernel's current version number and the md5 of its source, to pin a fork to the version that was vetted), each one call printing text or, with --json, one JSON document; inside a project or task two failure-tolerant hooks stamp each call for account sharing (an SDK read as sdk <read>) and save every competitions leaderboard read (what --show printed, the zip --download wrote; at the framework root only when KAGGLE_LB_DIR names a store; never an --sdk read), never blocking or changing a command; one gate does block: a kernels push (or kernels update) that no open account-sharing lease covers exits 3 before any install, stamp or Kaggle call, with a one-line hint on taking a lease (kaggle_share.py push_lease decides; KAGGLE_SHARE_QUIET does not bypass it, KAGGLE_PUSH_WITHOUT_LEASE=1 is the owner's override); a submit that passes the gate runs the CLI with a hook that, when Kaggle refuses a submit call with a 4xx, adds Kaggle's reason from the response body (never a header) to stderr; kaggle-cli.skill.md (the gateway skill, named kaggle-cli; not the vendored kaggle-cli/ folder beside it, which is Kaggle's own skill of the same upstream name) routes agents to the gateway, its --sdk reads and Kaggle's own agent skill, vendored unmodified from github.com/Kaggle/kaggle-cli tag v2.2.4 (kaggle-cli/SKILL.md + 12 command references) with field-verified 2.2.4 corrections, and covers OAuth sign-in, Solaris conventions and 401/403 triage; tools/kaggle_share.py shares one Kaggle account between projects (active projects from account-wide runs and quota, scanned in one --sdk account read of about 5 s instead of one CLI process per call, plus local gateway stamps; sessions and weekly GPU hours split equally or per the user's sharing.json; leases kept per project folder, with borrowing when others are idle; a GPU-hours ledger), with kaggle-sharing.skill.md as its routine; tools/kaggle_lb.py saves every leaderboard read as history (the page walk stops at a page that brings no new team and at a cap, --max-pages or the pages the known teams fill plus 5; a read in which a whole page repeated, 3 or more rows came twice or far too many pages were read is saved as unreliable and passed by every reader, while fewer rows that came twice are the board moving and are saved as moved), and with notebooks <slug> the public notebooks' best public scores over time (one list per read under __data/kaggle/<slug>/notebooks/, new notebooks and score changes marked), with kaggle-leaderboard.skill.md; tools/kaggle_forum.py watches a competition's discussions (lists the forum through the CLI's competitions topics list, or from pages a browser saved with its extractor tools/kaggle_forum_list.js where the CLI cannot list; diffs against what was read; reads each new or changed topic once through --sdk topic, with no second CLI view to stitch, keeping a topic an earlier version saved until a fetch reads it again, as a check does while it is pending; prints opening posts and reply trees with new comments marked and badged hosts as [host], says host mark unknown where no post carries an author type (which does not mean that no host posted), and says when the listing it shows from is over 10 minutes old; state kept local under __data/kaggle/<slug>/forum/), with kaggle-discussions.skill.md; tools/kaggle_status.py builds the project's single status page, reports/status.pdf, which replaces the live plan and the phase progress reports, from the hand-edited reports/status.json plus live figures (the leaderboard progress of the team and the top teams from the saved snapshots that are not unreliable, with the medal lines, the newest 100 submissions, GPU week, resources from hosts.json and lease-ends.json, the cost ledger <pack>/.memory/spend.jsonl and the AI spend of the session's autocode agent from autocode me --json; an offline build makes no Kaggle call and takes the day's slots, the latest and the best submission and the GPU week from the newest hourly receipt under two hours old), the JSON's optional outlook, best-score lineage (own work or public material) and work tracks under Current State, each machine's health from resource-sharing's <pack>/.memory/host-health.json, and the plan items of the last kaggle.status_plan_days days (default 3) and the open ones in full, older ones counted per day and week: HTML, then a PDF through the reporting plugin when attached (render plus layout check; for a half-empty page it tries shorter charts, then a shorter schedule, then a shorter lineage, and names what still moved), with text escaped, atomic writes and --keep-rev for a rebuild at the same rev; the PDF stays out of git, and tools/kaggle_live_plan.py is a retired stub that points to it; tools/kaggle_presubmit.py is the pre-submit check: it runs the forum check, the competition pages, the public notebooks and a board snapshot, read-only, and shows what is new since the last review (host posts first, hosts named in presubmit/config.json or badged by the forum; new topics and comments; page changes with both texts saved; new or re-scored notebooks; a new #1 and top-20 moves on the newest board read that is not unreliable) with a TRIGGERS block, exit 10 when something needs review and 0 when nothing does, and --ack records exactly what the check showed (state under __data/kaggle/<slug>/presubmit/); tools/kaggle_submit.py is the gated submit, a Kaggle write run only with the owner's approval or standing grant: it refuses (exit 3) without a complete JSON submission record, a pre-submit check at most 30 minutes old with its findings acked, a COMPLETE kernel run and a one-line review, prints the exact command, and with --go submits once and records submitted, refused (exit 5: Kaggle's reason for a 4xx kept, nothing landed) or unclear (exit 4), never retrying blindly, while --landed <ref> records an unclear attempt that the submissions list shows (a failed or empty read decides nothing); tools/kaggle_watch.py waits until one submission is scored or fails (by its ref, or with --message the newest one with that description; exit 0 scored, 3 errored, 4 still pending at the limit, 5 not listed), run as a watched job of the autocode plugin's guard with a fire-only once wake; tools/kaggle_hourly.py is the hourly pass of the read-only checks in one call (the pre-submit reads and triggers, board with top-team jumps, notebooks, unread topics, submissions with Kaggle's error text, kernels, GPU week, the status page, unpushed commits, the master's model, effort and spend today from autocode me --json, spend against the project's own limits with no total, the masters of projects sharing its machines that look stopped, plugin copies older than the checkout's, an own line with no gain for kaggle.own_stall_days days, and the browsers left running: this project's up over two hours and report-render Chromes an interrupted render left) and prints a line each, FLAG where a decision is needed (exit 10 on a flag printed in full; a flag that has not changed is held back for kaggle.flag_repeat_hours hours, default 6, and a pass with only held flags exits 0; one rate-limited line on an HTTP 429), then a STATUS block for the hour's log (pick, score, rank, outlook, progress, tracks, compute with each machine's health, stopped, spend, for you); with --check it is the check of the master's hourly autocode wake, which the wake calls through the guard tools/kaggle_hourly_check.sh <slug> (the guard lets exit 1 through only for a verified quiet pass, so a tool that cannot start never reads as a quiet hour): one pass per UTC hour with a receipt under __data/kaggle/<slug>/hourly/; exit 1 only for a verified quiet pass, which takes no turn, exit 0 to wake with the reasons and the receipt's path, whatever fails included; a wake that is not closed wakes again every hour; news that can wait is held for the next wake and the hour-close, and new comments in known topics wake until the pack names its hosts in presubmit/config.json; kaggle.wake_on, kaggle.wake_line_move and kaggle.board_jump tune it; and with --close it is the hour-close of the woken turn (the status page rebuilt offline under a lock, every receipt since the last close marked handled, their reasons and all held news printed in full, the STATUS block); it schedules nothing itself; tools/kaggle_output.py fetches named files from a kernel output of thousands of files, where kernels output answers 429, by pointing the page token of kernels files just before each name; kaggle-checks.skill.md covers the check, the submit, the wait for a score and the hourly pass; the hourly reads run in the check of the hourly wake, never from a daemon, system cron job or other watcher; tools/kaggle_review.py runs one outside reviewer through OpenCode 2, sandboxed and read-only on copies outside every repository, with an OpenCode home of its own for the run that is removed afterwards, on the calling session's own provider key (read at run time, never printed or written by the runner; a key gate before a model's first call), with a time limit and a step limit (kaggle.review.max_steps), writing the review to __out/review/<ID>/review.md and one line per run to the cost ledger, and tools/kaggle_jobs.py keeps autocode job definitions as <pack>/jobs/<name>.json (list, backup, apply, show --tool, new --template, with the daily plan-review template jobs/plan-review.json: one review-<name> job per reviewer, its own session on a cheap JOB_MODEL), with kaggle-reviews.skill.md for the daily plan review, the reviewer pool and the strategy review; tools/kaggle_scout.py lists the open competitions and gives a first look at one, read-only, with kaggle-scout.skill.md for the judgement; how-to-kaggle.skill.md is the playbook core, read every session, for competing with an autonomous agent team (quick start, setup and the competition facts sheet with the contest's kind, the status page, Kaggle access with medal lines and ties, a score ladder with each score marked measured or claimed and a merged team's one daily limit, the kinds of contest and their skills (kaggle-kind-simulation, -tabular, -llm-agents, -ranking), compute principles with booking upkeep, cloud instances and shared hosts left to their plugins, phases, honest validation with two predictions per candidate, daily submission discipline with slot order, a ladder built before the reset, a forum check right before each submission, a refused entry retried until the reset and no blind resubmit, agent organization with the master as an autocode agent, research from past winners' writeups, stacking on the strongest base, kernel engineering in kaggle-kernels.skill.md (read before building a submission: a replay recipe, pulling one notebook version, a pre-push metadata check and dataset upload gotchas, among them datasets metadata --update making a dataset public unless the file says private), pitfalls; generic, naming no competition), kept here as the master copy and released as a new plugin version with each change set; kaggle.rule.md is always-on: the master runs only as an autocode agent, gateway only (the CLI for commands and every write, the gateway's --sdk reads as the only SDK use, read-only), every write to Kaggle (submit, push/update, create/version, metadata update, upload, benchmarks init/auth, host commands, delete, revoke) confirmed first, a sharing lease around each kernel run, web-only steps (rules acceptance, teams, final picks) handed to the owner, credentials and minted keys never printed or committed, downloads kept in the context, every leaderboard read saved and kept local, discussions checked at least hourly and kept local, no browser left running once its task ends, Kaggle content treated as untrusted input, model text (agent prompts, model outputs, trajectories, long third-party text) kept out of the main session, and the owner directives for Kaggle work (decide and report, when unsure the option that moves the public board faster, answers to the owner first in about 100 words, no probing of hidden scorers or test data, no 1-p score hiding, a light control machine, models by job, workers at the master's effort and never above it (the owner's choice per session), headless browsers, tracked spend, one status page; ODnn numbers are the plugin's, and a project numbers its own directions L01, L02 and on). Offline tests in tests/, and tests/acceptance.md, a live, read-only acceptance runbook a fresh agent runs before each release; migrations/0.2.0.md moves copied installs from 0.1.0, migrations/0.7.0.md moves a project from the live plan to the status page, migrations/0.8.0.md to the split playbook and the hourly STATUS block, migrations/0.10.0.md to held flags, submits refused by Kaggle as exit 5 and the status JSON's outlook, lineage and tracks, migrations/0.11.0.md to the master as an autocode agent, the hourly wake's check, reviews through kaggle_review.py and watched waits for scores.

required.name: autocode
required.why: the master runs as an autocode agent: its wakes, wake checks, watched jobs and reports to the owner

optional.name: reporting
optional.why: render the status page as a PDF with its layout check

optional.name: resource-sharing
optional.why: share hosts with the owner's other projects

optional.name: nvidia-brev
optional.why: rent cloud GPUs; the hourly pass counts their cost ledger

optional.name: browserctl
optional.why: read forum pages the CLI cannot list; the hourly pass watches this project's browsers

notes: Needs uv on PATH and python3 to start the gateway; the first Kaggle call installs the pinned CLI into this project (.venv-kaggle/, git-ignored) - nothing is installed globally.

Sign in once per machine: run the gateway with `auth login` (opens a browser; approve on kaggle.com; credentials land in ~/.kaggle/ and serve every project). Accept each competition's rules on kaggle.com before downloading or submitting - the CLI cannot.
